newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh reaches agreement with tribal rebels.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh reaches agreement with tribal rebels.

text.p: Bangladesh on Wednesday said it had reached agreement with tribal leaders to end a decades-old insurgency in southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts and soon would sign a peace deal.
"We have reached consensus on all issues. We are going to sign a peace deal very soon," chief government negotiator Abul Hasanat Abdullah told reporters in Dhaka.
Abdullah declined to say when the treaty between the government and tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas would be signed, or what it would contain.

But Kalparanjan Chakma, a ruling Awami League party legislator from the Hill Tracts and member of the government negotiating team, told reporters the deal was expected after Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was briefed on the outcome of four days of talks.
Hasina is due to return from a meeting of South Asian leaders in the Maldives on Wednesday night.
Over 8,500 civilians, rebels and soldiers have been killed in the insurgency started by the Shanti Bahini in 1973 over demand for autonomy of the Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma.
